description:
`dispatch_from_callsite_summary` (src/compiler2/callsite_dispatch.rs:18-45)
builds a multi-target callsite arm table by comparing
`runtime_type_test_envelope` of each target's `surface_inputs` and selecting the
columns where those envelopes differ (`discriminating_inputs`, :88-98). The
envelope and the runtime predicate disagree about what is observable, in BOTH
directions, and both directions produce an unsound plan.

## 1. The envelope ERASES a distinction that is semantically real

`runtime_type_test_envelope` (types/mod.rs:1232-1238) rewrites top-level
`descr.funcs` to `Descr::fun_top().funcs`. Two targets differing only by which
callable arrives compare EQUAL, no column is discriminating, every row gets empty
preconditions, and the plan degenerates to a constant: arm 0 swallows every call
and arms 1..n are dead.

## 2. The envelope PRESERVES a distinction the runtime cannot test

`runtime_list_sig` (types/mod.rs:2147-2154) keeps a list's element type, and
`runtime_tuple_sig` (:2138-2145) recurses through `runtime_envelope_ty`, which
does NOT collapse funcs. So `[integer]` vs `[atom]`, or `{:cont, fn_a}` vs
`{:cont, fn_b}`, DO get picked as discriminating columns. But
`runtime_type_predicate_list_shapes` (types/mod.rs:1950-1974) never reads `elem`
-- it projects only `ListShape { Empty, NonEmpty }` -- and
`runtime_type_predicate_tuple_arities` (:1976-1994) projects only arity. Both
arms compile to identical runtime tests, so arm 0 wins again.

Worse: a possibly-empty list of T (`ListSig { empty: true, elem: Some(T) }`) is
neither `is_exact_empty` nor `is_exact_non_empty` (sigs.rs:56-62), so it projects
to the fully permissive `{Empty, NonEmpty}` and `[]` satisfies EVERY
element-typed list test.

## This is not latent -- it ships in a green fixture

    $ ./target/debug/fz2 interp --dump backend=mf.backend \
        fixtures2/behavior/enum_map_family.fz
    $ grep -n DispatchCallEdge mf.backend
    38915: DispatchCallEdge {

That edge:

    arms: [ DispatchArm { id: ArmId(0), questions: [], ..., outcome: OutcomeId(0) },
            DispatchArm { id: ArmId(1), questions: [], ..., outcome: OutcomeId(1) } ]
    graph: DispatchGraph { nodes: [ Fail, Outcome { outcome: OutcomeId(0), ... } ],
                           root: GraphNodeId(1) }
    arms: [ DispatchCallArm { body_id: 0, callee: Local(104), ... },
            DispatchCallArm { body_id: 1, callee: Local(105), ... } ]
    miss: Unreachable

Two callees, ZERO questions, a constant graph root: `Local(105)` is unreachable
and `Local(104)` receives every call. enum_map_family is green today, so the arm
table is currently benign -- but it is a real invented arm table with a dead arm,
and nothing in the plan records that the discrimination is undecidable.

Other DispatchCallEdges in the corpus (enum_take_drop_split x4,
enum_predicate_search x4) do mint Region::Type questions, so the seam is
exercised both ways.

## What the old ticket got wrong

It claimed the envelope "preserves closure identity". At the TOP LEVEL of an
input it does not -- funcs collapse to fun_top, and
`callable_flow_dispatch_does_not_discriminate_unobservable_callable_correlations`
(callsite_dispatch.rs:305-377) deliberately PINS that erasure together with
first-arm selection. The surviving closure leak is callables NESTED under a tuple
or list, which the envelope does not collapse. It also called the seam "latent";
enum_map_family ships a question-less two-arm table at HEAD.

## Checks

- `dispatch_from_callsite_summary` never returns a plan whose arms are all
  question-less: either it discriminates at the PREDICATE projection
  (`Types::runtime_type_predicate`, types/mod.rs:1138) rather than at the
  envelope Ty, or it returns `Ok(None)` / a loud error so the callsite falls back
  to value-identity dispatch on the callable column.
- A precondition column is selected only when the two targets'
  `runtime_type_predicate` projections actually differ. Regression: two targets
  whose surface inputs are `[integer]` and `[atom]` must NOT produce a
  Region::Type arm table.
- `[]` does not satisfy an element-typed list precondition minted by this path.
- Re-dump enum_map_family / enum_predicate_search / enum_take_drop_split and
  assert every DispatchCallEdge has at least one arm question per non-default
  arm.
- Full lib + matrix green.

Not an Elixir-semantics question: this is a compiler-internal dispatch-plan
defect with no Elixir-visible construct that names it.
title: Multi-target callsite dispatch mints arm tables the runtime predicate cannot decide; question-less arms collapse to arm 0
